guide.summary: Public agent using your own Harvest OAuth app (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).
guide.verdict: Public agent using your own Harvest OAuth app (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).

composio.note: Harvest is listed under Composio-managed OAuth. For production, create an auth config with your own client ID and secret, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio supplies a managed Harvest app. For production you will likely want your own, so users see your app name and you get dedicated quota.
reasons: Users see your app name instead of 'Composio wants to access your account'
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own app gets dedicated quota
Managed default scopes may not cover everything you need
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for polling triggers

scenarios.label: Public agent using your own Harvest OAuth app
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent connects many customers' Harvest accounts through an OAuth2 app you register in Harvest ID.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; see c3, c5

waiting.basis: The V2 docs describe registering the app but no review step (c1). No wait time was documented.

scenarios.approval: No review is described in the Harvest V2 docs; apps for other users just need a registered OAuth2 Application. This is inferred from absence, so confirm with Harvest.
extras: Administrator login needed to register the app

modifiers.note: Administrator login needed to register the app

prerequisites.title: Harvest administrator login
prerequisites.detail: Registering an OAuth app needs an Administrator login on a Harvest account. This comes from older V1 docs, so check it still holds for Harvest ID.

prerequisites.title: Decide Harvest/Forecast products and account mode
prerequisites.detail: Choose the products (Harvest, Forecast or both) and whether the app supports multiple accounts, and pick the minimal scope.

steps.title: Decide products and account mode
steps.detail: Draft the app name, products and multi-account setting, using the minimal scope that works.
inputs: Which Harvest features the agent needs
steps.done_when: Settings list is ready to enter

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio dashboard
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard for the Harvest auth config. Any redirect_uri sent later must start with the registered Redirect URL.

steps.title: Create OAuth2 app in Harvest ID
steps.detail: Log in as an administrator and create the application in the Developers section of Harvest ID. Enter name, Redirect URL, multi-account setting and products.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and client secret

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the Harvest auth config through Composio's API using your own client ID and secret.

steps.title: Test a connection end to end
steps.detail: Connect a Harvest account, authorize it, and run a tool call. Check that the consent screen shows your app name.
steps.done_when: Connected account works and tool calls succeed

traps.title: The page describes end users being redirected to Harvest
traps.detail: The page describes end users being redirected to Harvest to authorize their own accounts with the application; it does not mention an admin approval step.

traps.title: Greenhouse 'Harvest API' is a different product
traps.detail: Search results about Greenhouse's Harvest API describe a signed partner agreement and monthly reviews. That applies to Greenhouse, not to Harvest time tracking, so do not plan around it.

traps.title: Some Harvest docs are legacy
traps.detail: The V1 API is deprecated, and one cited GitHub copy of the OAuth docs was archived in 2019. Follow the V2 / Harvest ID docs.

traps.title: Rate limits can block accounts
traps.detail: General API limit is 100 requests per 15 seconds and Reports API is 100 per 15 minutes. Exceeding them returns HTTP 429, and abusing the API may get you blocked.

traps.title: Access tokens expire after 18 hours
traps.detail: A reported (older, archived) source says each user's token expires after 18 hours, so plan for token refresh. Verify against current docs.

blockers.symptom: Consent screen says 'Composio wants to access your account'
blockers.what_it_means: You are using the managed app, not your own.
blockers.what_to_do: Register your own Harvest OAuth2 app and use it in a Composio auth config.
blockers.agent_can_help: Create the auth config through Composio's API once you have the credentials.

open_questions: Does Harvest review or restrict OAuth2 apps used by outside customers? None found; ask Harvest support or test with a second organization's account.
Are there user or install caps on unreviewed apps? Not found; check the Harvest ID Developers page or ask support.
Is the 18-hour token expiry still current? It comes from an archived source; test a token's lifetime or check current docs.
Is there an optional listing in Harvest's integration directory? A submission form exists, but whether it is required or reviewed was not confirmed.
Not found: what each review or verification checks and what the developer must submit. Checked getharvest.com, getharvest.com.
